title: Co-sponsor evidence from Laura's real audience (Taiwan), not only U.S. funders
brief: RULES (same as the main review): Today is Fri 16 Oct 2026 (Sydney). Team Caplet (Knox Grammar, Sydney; six students, first names only) in the Wharton Global High School Investment Competition 2026-27; client Laura Gao (real person; contacting her is banned). Repo /home/user/caplet-investment and /home/user/caplet-latest are READ-ONLY (no edits, no git commit/push). Cite every claim as repo path:line or URL + 'accessed 16 Oct 2026'; anything not verified is labelled UNVERIFIED; label numbers MARKET / MODEL / ASSUMPTION with basis and date. Do NOT draft Trading Notes reflections, IPS text, the pitch, fundraising text or Final Report prose: give knowledge, evidence, numbers, checklists. No personal data (no surnames, emails, WInS username/account, birthdays); never rank teammates; never contact anyone, post, submit or log in. Plain English, short sentences. Fetch pages with: python3 oct16/tools/page.py URL [--grep "exact phrase"]; plain curl works for many sites; the WebSearch tool works (load it with ToolSearch 'select:WebSearch'; snippets alone are UNVERIFIED); WebFetch is blocked. WHAT IS MISSING. The 2026-27 rubric now scores communicating 'Laura's potential facility contribution and investment uncertainty clearly and credibly to prospective co-sponsors' (competition/official/2026_27/smapply_public_2026-10-14/deliverables.txt:59) and tailoring to her 'residency goals' (:56). The case puts the residency in Taiwan (Laura_Gao_2026_Client_Profile.txt:76-80), names co-sponsors, grants, collaborators and program fees as other money (:85-86), sets the 2031 range task (:109-120) and requires each team to 'draft part of Laura's fundraising materials' (:123-124). All of Caplet's funder evidence is U.S.: Kresge (2011 guide), SSIR, U.S. field experiments (team/google_drive/notes_and_discussions.md:211-220). The verified lens findings say so: oct16/verify/L04_uniqueness.final.json UNIQ-05 ('mostly U.S. individual donors or one U.S. foundation, not Taiwanese institutional co-sponsors') and L04-V1 (the Kresge note is misread). A grep of the repo and all 12 lens files on 16 Oct found no Taiwan funder source at all. WHAT TO CHECK (time-box about 2 hours). (1) Primary Taiwan sources on public or institutional support for artist residencies / artist villages, read ONLY for how a funder judges a founder's own pledged contribution: is a self-funding share or match required; what proof counts (pledge letter, proof of funds); currency (NT$ vs US$); single-year vs multi-year commitments; application timing relative to 2031-2033. Leads: the Ministry of Culture's Artist Residency Network Taiwan (https://artres.moc.gov.tw/en/about/), which a WebSearch snippet on 16 Oct described as running the 'MOC Operation Directions for Sponsoring Artist Villages' (snippet only, UNVERIFIED); the National Culture and Arts Foundation grant rules; city culture bureau residency programmes (Taipei, Tainan). Access on 16 Oct from this sandbox: moc.gov.tw and law.moc.gov.tw returned HTTP 403; english.moc.gov.tw and en.ncafroc.org.tw were refused by the proxy; web.archive.org CDX is blocked; transartists.org loads (200). Try other mirrors, PDFs found by search, and English secondary sources (Res Artis, TransArtists, peer-reviewed papers). (2) Whether anything found changes the fundraising-text checklist already proposed in oct16/verify/L02_client_forensic.final.json CLIENT-12 and CLIENT-10 (range in US$ vs NT$, firm vs conditional pledge, quote date, re-quote rule) and UNIQ-05. (3) If primary pages stay unreadable, build a short student reading list (3-5 URLs the students can open themselves from Sydney, each with the exact question to answer). That turns this into student-owned research, which also helps the 'authentic team voice' criterion. SCOPE GUARD: the case says teams need not estimate facility cost, a construction budget, the funding gap or a business plan, nor Taiwan legal and regulatory requirements (Laura_Gao_2026_Client_Profile.txt:164-169). Do not size any gap, cost or contingency fund (case:106-107). Only how co-sponsors read a founder's pledge. Do not draft any fundraising text. Do not contact any Taiwanese body. OUTPUT (write only under oct16/gaps/G1_taiwan_cosponsors/): findings.json (list of findings in the verify schema: id, title, severity, deliverables, problem, evidence, fix, confidence, new_vs_known, deadline); evidence_card.md (one page: each usable fact with exact quote, URL, access date, and scope = country, year, funder type, VERIFIED/UNVERIFIED; plus a 'do not claim' list of statements the team must not make without a source); student_reading_list.md. Success test: a student can answer 'Why would a Taiwanese co-sponsor believe Laura's range?' with one sourced fact, or honestly say 'no source found; we rely on the case's own logic'. Deadline relevance: Final Report 4 Dec (Sat 5 Dec 09:00 Sydney); the IPS needs only the principle (2026_WGY_Investment_Policy-FINAL.txt:68-70 says the IPS is not expected to include the co-sponsor communication).

brief: RULES (same as the main review): Today is Fri 16 Oct 2026 (Sydney). Team Caplet (Knox Grammar, Sydney; six students, first names only) in the Wharton Global High School Investment Competition 2026-27; client Laura Gao (real person; contacting her is banned). WHAT IS MISSING. Every Global Finale panel 2022-2026 had an Aberdeen judge; in 2024 a fixed-income specialist and in 2025 and 2026 a 'U.S. Credit Investment Manager' (oct16/research/KB_what_wins.md:181). The rubric scores 'uses appropriate diversification' (smapply_public_2026-10-14/deliverables.txt:55). On the holdings basis the payment ladder cost $298,628 on the 15 Oct curve, leaving about $1,372 (4.7bp) under $300k (KB_what_wins.md:432). A credit specialist's obvious question is: why not buy the payments with investment-grade corporate bonds for extra yield, or spread across other issuers? The lenses defend 'one issuer' only with Wharton's 'funding purposes' wording (oct16/verify/L06_ips_attack.final.json VA-1; L04 UNIQ-07; L01 JUDGE-05; L12 PM-15) and the likely-question list (oct16/lenses/L07_final_report_foresight.md:291, Q12). No lens prices the within-rules alternatives. The team's rejection exists only as words (decisions/03_reserve_composition.md:16 'Default and downgrade risk conflicts with the certainty mandate'; :46) and one superseded estimate (research/insight_v1/phase_B/B4b_practice_benchmark.md:284-298: '$16k-22k less than $292,264' at 58-79bp spread, on the STRIPS basis that the 6 Oct Wharton email retired, less a J.P. Morgan 'approximately 50 basis points' a year downgrade-and-default drag from Oct 2021). RULES ON INSTRUMENTS: 'Any Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) available on WInS' and 'Any Government/Treasury Bonds from any exchange available on WInS' are permitted for both contributions (smapply_public_2026-10-14/faqs.txt:42-45); derivatives are banned (:51), so the team cannot hedge currency itself; FX conversion is automatic (trading.txt:38). The public Trading Details page lists Treasury bonds from the 'United States, United Kingdom, Germany, France, Italy, and the Netherlands' (trading.txt:46), but COMPETITION.md:77 records that the logged-in session rules and the 6 Oct email say U.S. Treasuries: record this conflict, do not resolve it by assumption. WHAT TO COMPUTE AND CHECK. (a) Corporate alternative on the holdings basis: reprice the ten $50,000 payments at Caplet's holding maturities on the latest treasury.gov curve (caplet-latest/competition/official_market_data/daily-treasury-rates_2026-10.csv) with a flat spread added, reusing oct16/research/KB_verify/num/reconcile.py or scratchpad/oct14/factcheck/ladder.py. Spreads: ICE BofA US Corporate OAS 0.84% and AA OAS 0.60% on 14 Oct 2026 (FRED BAMLC0A0CM, BAMLC0A2CAA, fetched 16 Oct 2026 with curl --http1.1 'https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=BAMLC0A0CM,BAMLC0A2CAA'). Report gross saving in dollars, an expected downgrade/default drag from a current primary source if one can be found (else mark the 2021 figure as old), and a plain worst case (which payment is lost if one issuer defaults, given fund diversification). (b) Which iShares iBonds Dec-20xx Term Corporate ETFs cover 2032-2041, with fees and yields from ishares.com fund pages (the site loads; WInS listing is a student check: the assistant cannot log in). (c) Non-U.S. government bonds: size the currency risk to a US$ promise with public EUR/USD and GBP/USD volatility; note that only a currency-hedged ETF could remove it (whether such an ETF is allowed is an interpretation: UNVERIFIED). (d) Link, do not redo, TIPS (oct16/verify/L03_strategy_redteam.final.json STRAT-14). Note: the strategy freezes on 6 Nov and decisions belong to the students; do not recommend a change unless the numbers show a clear error. OUTPUT (write only under oct16/gaps/G2_credit_alternatives/): findings.json (verify schema as above); considered_rejected.md = one table: alternative | dollars saved or added on the holdings basis, with date | which payment's certainty it puts at risk and how | rule status (allowed? WInS-listed? UNVERIFIED) | one plain-English reason a student could say; plus 3-5 likely credit-judge questions with the evidence each answer needs (no prose answers); plus the script and results file. Success test: a student can say in one sentence, with a dated dollar figure, what the extra corporate yield would buy and what it would put at risk. Deadline relevance: the reason belongs in the Final Report (4 Dec) alternatives table (oct16/verify/L07_final_report_foresight.final.json FR-17) and in finale Q&A; the IPS carries at most one principle.
